extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), OED staff, and adjudicators in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria used in USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline (OED) proceedings to determine practitioner misconduct and appropriate sanctions (suspension, restitution, reinstatement). Includes applicable regulatory provisions, burden of proof, sanctioning factors, and procedural rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof (clear and convincing evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director has the burden of proving alleged violations by clear and convincing evidence. Respondent must prove any affirmative defense by clear and convincing evidence. 37 C.F.R. § 11.49.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard of proof for both prosecution and defensive affirmative claims in USPTO disciplinary proceedings; decisive finding must be supported by clear and convincing proof of misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to suspend or exclude practitioners (35 U.S.C. § 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO has the exclusive authority to establish qualifications for admitting persons to practice before it, and to suspend or exclude them from practicing before it. The Director may suspend or exclude a person if shown to be incompetent or disreputable, or guilty of gross misconduct, or if the person violates Office regulations. 35 U.S.C. § 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory basis for disciplinary jurisdiction and the scope of sanctions (suspension/exclusion) against patent practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(1) — Violate a Disciplinary Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not: (1) Violate a Disciplinary Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation of any disciplinary rule is itself proscribed conduct and may support sanctioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(2) — Circumvent a Disciplinary Rule through actions of another
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not: (2) Circumvent a Disciplinary Rule through actions of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct that attempts to avoid professional responsibilities by using third parties is prohibited and may be sanctionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) — Engage in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not: (3) Engage in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal/illegal acts involving moral turpitude are grounds for discipline; severity depends on nature and relation to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — Engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not: (4) Engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dishonest acts (e.g., misrepresenting status of filings, providing false statements about payments) are serious aggravating misconduct that commonly leads to suspension or exclusion; examples and case citations in the decision demonstrate heightened severity where client harm or obstruction of process occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — Engage in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not: (5) Engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to perform duties that impair the functioning of the Office (e.g., causing abandonment of client application through nonpayment) falls under this prohibition and supports discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — Catch-all: conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not: (6) Engage in any other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad residual prohibition; however, conduct already encompassed by subsections (1)-(5) cannot also be charged under (6) (i.e., (6) is not duplicative). Used for conduct not falling neatly into prior subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to properly remit client funds / submitting declined payment forms (Count I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation that respondent, having received client filing fees, repeatedly submitted a debit card authorization that was declined by the bank, and thus failed to properly or timely remit funds from a client to the Office (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b) via 10.23(c)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific misconduct: accepting client funds and failing to ensure payment to the USPTO; evaluated by proof of received client funds, attempted payment attempts, bank records, and resulting client harm (abandonment). Repeated failed debits and lack of adequate funds are strong evidence of violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenting unprocessable payment forms / misrepresentation about payment attempts (Count II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation that respondent engaged in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation by repeatedly presenting to the USPTO a form of payment that could not be processed (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether practitioner knowingly or recklessly presented ineffective payment methods and/or misled the Office or client about payment efforts; false explanations (e.g., blaming bank without corroboration) aggravate sanction severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice by failing to submit payment (Count III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation that respondent's repeated failure to timely submit proper payment of required filing fees to the USPTO ultimately resulted in the client's patent application going abandoned (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on the effect of practitioner's omissions on the Office's processes and on third parties (applicants); abandonment of an application is a concrete prejudicial outcome supporting discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of a legal matter / failure to advise client (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c)) (Count IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) by failing to properly reply to Office actions and/or to ensure timely payment of filing fees, resulting in abandonment; also by failing to advise his client that filing fees had not been timely paid or that the application had been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates practitioner's duty of competent representation and communication: neglect (failure to act/respond) and failure to inform client of material developments are independent bases for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability of separate charge under 10.23(b)(6) when conduct fits earlier subsections (Count V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10.23(b)(6) is a 'catch all'; any alleged conduct that violates provisions (1)-(5) cannot also violate (6). The Complaint did not allege conduct beyond Counts 1-4, so Count 5 was not sustained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides charge drafting and evaluation: avoid duplicative charging under the catch-all when specific subsections already cover the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning factor — violation of duties owed (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: First factor: whether the practitioner has violated a duty owed to a client, to the public, to the legal system, and/or to the profession. 37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess specific duties breached (e.g., remit funds, communicate, competence) and weight the breach in determining sanction severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning factor — mental state (intentional/knowing/negligent) (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Second factor: whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently. 37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent or knowing misconduct and affirmative deception aggravate sanctions; negligence supports discipline but may justify lesser sanctions than deliberate misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning factor — actual or potential injury (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Third factor: the amount of the actual or potential injury caused by the practitioner's misconduct. 37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate client harm (e.g., abandonment, financial loss), harm to legal process, or potential wider impact to determine proportionality of sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning factor — aggravating or mitigating circumstances (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Fourth factor: the existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors. 37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider obstruction of proceedings, false statements, lack of remorse, prior discipline (aggravators) versus prompt restitution, cooperation, remorse (mitigators) in sizing sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating factors identified: obstruction, false statements, lack of remorse
rubrics_metrics.description: Obstruction of disciplinary process (failure to comply with investigation requests, misidentifying bank, failure to produce records), providing false information during proceeding, and failing to acknowledge wrongful conduct or show remorse are significant aggravating factors (cases cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such aggravating conduct can elevate sanction to suspension or exclusion; courts treat false statements and obstruction as 'extremely serious' and as analogous to misappropriation in severity assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating consideration: restitution and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Restitution to a client (making the client whole) and other mitigating circumstances can reduce sanction severity; but delayed, partial, or insincere restitution may have little mitigating effect. In this case restitution was ordered as the difference between amounts paid by the client to revive the application and amounts refunded by respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether restitution was timely, complete, and voluntary; appropriate restitution formula may be used to calculate amount owed (case used $945 - $540 = $405). Delays and failure to reimburse promptly reduce mitigating weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of discipline: protect public and preserve integrity (not punishment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary purpose of imposing professional discipline is not to punish, but to protect the public and preserve the integrity of the profession; sanctions should deter similar misconduct. (Discussion/Conclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions should be tailored to protect the public, preserve professional integrity, and deter recurrence—while considering proportionality and rehabilitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties while suspended and reinstatement procedure (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58, 11.60(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties while suspended) and remains suspended until the OED Director grants a petition reinstating the respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspended practitioners must follow regulatory obligations while suspended; reinstatement requires a successful petition and compliance with procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal rights (37 C.F.R. § 11.55(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days of the initial decision, either party may appeal to the USPTO Director. 37 C.F.R. § 11.55(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the procedural deadline and route for appellate review of initial disciplinary decisions.
